title: 2026 U.S. State Sales Tax Guide for SaaS Businesses
summary: Find state SaaS sales tax guides and official sources. Review product taxability, nexus, customer location, marketplace sales, registration, and filing.
body_markdown:
A SaaS sales tax review has two separate questions: is this sale taxable, and does your business have a duty to collect? Answer both for each state where you operate or sell.


Start with what the customer buys, how you deliver it, and where the customer uses it. Then review your business presence, sales history, and sales channels. A general sales tax rate or a product label such as “SaaS” does not settle every part of that review.


## Who should use this guide?


Use this guide if you sell hosted software, subscriptions, or API services across state lines. The state directory below links to detailed articles and tax authorities so you can review each location separately.


For an AI product, begin with the[AI agents and API sales tax guide](https://www.afternoon.co/blog/ai-agents-agentic-workflow-sales-tax) . It explains the facts to collect about software access, data services, and custom work before choosing a tax category.


## What is sales tax?


Sales tax applies to covered transactions under state and local rules. Sellers with a collection duty charge the applicable tax and remit it to the relevant authority.


Keep these parts of the review separate:


Question What to record


What is the product? Software rights, delivery method, services, and contract terms


Where does the sale or use occur? Customer location and any required user-location evidence


Must you collect? Business presence, sales history, and the jurisdiction's current rules


Does an exemption apply? The legal basis and required customer evidence


Who collects? Your company, a marketplace, or another party under the applicable rules


How will you report? Registration, filing schedule, invoice records, and credits


Do not use a statewide headline rate as the answer for every software invoice. For example,[Colorado software rules](https://tax.colorado.gov/sites/tax/files/02.2021_SUTT_Computer%20Software.pdf) distinguish delivery methods, and home-rule cities can require a separate review. Our[Colorado guide](https://www.afternoon.co/blog/colorado-sales-tax-guide) links to the[Denver guide](https://www.afternoon.co/blog/denver-city-sales-tax-guide) for that city-level distinction.


Talk to a sales tax expert


Get guidance tailored to your business

Choose a state to open its guide, then use the tax authority's current guidance to confirm the treatment for your product and customer. The directory covers all states and the District of Columbia. These rounded general rates help compare locations; they do not determine tax on a SaaS invoice. Average combined rates are not address-specific rates.

## Economic nexus thresholds (2026)


Economic nexus rules can require a remote seller to collect tax even without a physical presence. Review the state's current rule and your own business activity before deciding when to register.


For each state, record:


- Which sales count toward the threshold.
- The period used to measure those sales.
- Whether a transaction count applies.
- How marketplace sales enter the calculation.
- When collection must begin after the threshold is met.
- Whether physical presence creates a separate duty.


The form of the threshold matters. This reference covers the states reviewed in detail below; each linked guide explains the sales included, marketplace rules, and collection start date.


State Remote-seller threshold Measurement period Scope to check


[Alabama](https://www.afternoon.co/blog/alabama-sales-tax-guide) More than $250,000 in direct retail sales Prior calendar year Includes taxable and nontaxable retail sales; excludes qualifying wholesale and collecting SSUT marketplace sales.


[Colorado](https://www.afternoon.co/blog/colorado-sales-tax-guide) More than $100,000 in retail sales Current or prior calendar year Includes exempt retail sales. Review collecting marketplaces and home-rule cities separately.


[Connecticut](https://www.afternoon.co/blog/connecticut-sales-tax-guide) At least $100,000 **and** at least 200 retail sales 12 months ending September 30 before the assessed period Both tests must hold under the covered-sales rules. Do not use a calendar-year test.


[Florida](https://www.afternoon.co/blog/florida-sales-tax-guide) More than $100,000 in taxable remote sales Prior calendar year Covers tangible property ordered remotely and shipped into Florida; do not count nontaxable hosted software as taxable remote sales.


[Indiana](https://www.afternoon.co/blog/indiana-sales-tax-guide) More than $100,000 in covered gross revenue Current or prior calendar year No transaction-count test. Review the service-only exception and exclude facilitator-collected marketplace sales from the seller test.


[Iowa](https://www.afternoon.co/blog/iowa-sales-tax-guide) $100,000 or more in gross revenue Current or prior calendar year Includes exempt, wholesale/resale, and marketplace sales. An exemption from tax on a sale does not remove it from this test.


[Kentucky](https://www.afternoon.co/blog/kentucky-sales-tax-guide) More than $100,000 in gross sales **or** at least 200 transactions Current or prior calendar year Review collecting marketplaces separately from direct sales and retain the platform records.


[Louisiana](https://www.afternoon.co/blog/louisiana-sales-tax-guide) More than $100,000 in covered sales Current or prior calendar year Covers property, digital products, and services. The old transaction-count test no longer applies.


[Maryland](https://www.afternoon.co/blog/maryland-sales-tax-guide) More than $100,000 in sales **or** at least 200 transactions Current or prior calendar year Includes exempt and marketplace sales. A collecting marketplace can change which party must register and collect.


[Massachusetts](https://www.afternoon.co/blog/massachusetts-sales-tax-guide) More than $100,000 in sales Current and prior calendar years No transaction-count test. Exclude facilitator-collected sales from the seller threshold and check the collection start date.


[Minnesota](https://www.afternoon.co/blog/minnesota-sales-tax-guide) More than $100,000 in retail sales **or** at least 200 retail transactions Prior 12 months Includes direct and marketplace retail sales; excludes documented resale sales.


[Ohio](https://www.afternoon.co/blog/ohio-sales-tax-guide) More than $100,000 in covered gross receipts **or** at least 200 transactions Current or prior calendar year Review the covered receipts and each channel’s collector; this is not a rolling 12-month test.


[Pennsylvania](https://www.afternoon.co/blog/pennsylvania-sales-tax-guide) More than $100,000 in sales Prior calendar year Includes taxable and nontaxable sales; excludes facilitator-collected marketplace sales for the remote seller. Collection for this test starts April 1.


[Tennessee](https://www.afternoon.co/blog/tennessee-sales-tax-guide) $100,000 or more in retail sales Prior 12 months Includes exempt retail sales; excludes resale. Review the collecting-marketplace exception separately.


[Virginia](https://www.afternoon.co/blog/virginia-sales-tax-guide) More than $100,000 in gross retail sales **or** at least 200 retail transactions Current or prior calendar year A seller using a collecting marketplace tests its direct sales outside that marketplace.


Physical presence can create a separate duty below these amounts. Crossing a sales threshold does not make an exempt product taxable. For other states, use the full state directory above or the[Streamlined Sales Tax state directory](https://www.streamlinedsalestax.org/for-businesses/remote-seller-faqs/remote-seller-state-guidance) . Check the state’s current rule when a summary and the authority differ.


Keep the sales report and source used for that decision. A threshold in a summary table is not enough if your report counts a different set of sales or uses a different period.


For a worked state review, see[Pennsylvania's online retailer guidance](https://www.pa.gov/agencies/revenue/resources/tax-types-and-information/sales-use-and-hotel-occupancy-tax/online-retailers) and our[Pennsylvania SaaS guide](https://www.afternoon.co/blog/pennsylvania-sales-tax-guide) . Apply the relevant state's own rule when reviewing another location.


## Filing, deadlines & penalties


After registration, record the account number, effective date, assigned filing schedule, and payment method. Confirm whether the account requires returns for periods with no tax due.


Reconcile customer charges, refunds, credits, exempt sales, and marketplace-collected amounts before filing. Keep tax collected separate from revenue and match the return to the supporting transaction records.


Use the authority's instructions for late returns, corrections, and relief requests. A single national deadline or penalty percentage would hide differences between accounts and jurisdictions.


For the invoice records, see[B2B SaaS invoicing](https://www.afternoon.co/blog/invoicing-B2B-SaaS) . For the system setup, use[sales tax software for AI and API companies](https://www.afternoon.co/blog/sales-tax-software-ai-api-companies) to test the path from a tax decision to an invoice and return.


## FAQs: U.S. Sales Tax


### Does the U.S. have a federal sales tax?


There is no general federal sales tax. Review state and local sales taxes separately from federal income tax and any product-specific federal taxes.


### What is economic nexus?


It is a collection duty that can arise from a seller's economic activity in a state even without physical presence. The amount, transaction test, sales included, and measurement period vary. A business with physical presence needs a separate review even below a remote-seller threshold.


### Which states do not have a statewide sales tax?


Alaska, Delaware, Montana, New Hampshire, and Oregon have no general statewide sales tax. Alaska can impose local sales taxes. A zero statewide rate does not establish that a business owes no other state or local tax; use the official resource in the table for the location.


### Do states tax SaaS and digital products?


Some do, and the answer can depend on the rights sold, delivery method, customer use, and local rules. Use the state directory to find the relevant guidance rather than applying one answer across the country.


### Does a marketplace collect all my sales tax?


Review the specific channel and transaction. A platform's collection role does not automatically cover your direct website sales or settle every registration and filing duty. The[Apple App Store guide](https://www.afternoon.co/blog/apple-app-store-sales-tax-guide) and[Google Play guide](https://www.afternoon.co/blog/google-play-sales-tax-guide) explain how to keep those channels separate.


### How do I register for sales tax?


Start with the tax authority linked for the state. Confirm the duty and start date before applying, then keep the account details and filing schedule with your sales records.


### What should I do if I missed a filing?


Identify the account, period, and missing return or payment. Follow the authority's correction process and review any notice before making an adjustment. Turning collection on now does not settle prior periods.


### Does this cover Canadian customers?


Canadian sales need a separate review. Our[GST/HST guide for US SaaS companies](https://www.afternoon.co/blog/canadian-sales-tax-guide-for-US-SaaS-companies) explains the registration paths and why federal registration does not resolve every provincial tax question.
